# Verstappen wins rain-hit Bahrain GP in Malaysia over Antonelli as Russell retires late on
Max Verstappen claimed his and Red Bull’s first win of the 2026 season at the end of a dramatic, rain-delayed Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

Oct 04, 2026 10:38am UTC

![KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 04: Race winner Max Verstappen of the Netherlands and Oracle Red](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9North/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/trackside-images/2026/F1_Grand_Prix_of_Bahrain_in_Malaysia/2298510158.webp)

Max Verstappen converted pole position into victory during Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, which was impacted by heavy rain, featured an entertaining crossover from intermediate tyres to slicks, and saw overtaking from start to finish – as well as a dramatic late retirement for George Russell.

Polesitter Verstappen fell behind Mercedes pair Kimi Antonelli and Russell on the run down to Turn 1, with all three drivers running intermediate tyres, but he soon settled into a rhythm and managed to pick off the Silver Arrows either side of a Safety Car that was deployed when Valtteri Bottas spun out.

That Safety Car period represented the ideal window for the intermediate starters to switch to slick tyres, with those who lined up on slick compounds getting caught out, and threats of further rain not materialising before the chequered flag.

Race results

### AS IT HAPPENED
At the end of an entertaining Qualifying session around the Sepang International Circuit, it was Verstappen who grabbed his and Red Bull’s first pole position of the 2026 season, just ahead of Ferrari rival Hamilton.

But then, in the hour before lights out, a huge rain shower – and accompanying thunderstorm – soaked the circuit, adding a completely different dimension to the mix. Would the race get under way as planned?

So, some 40 minutes later than planned, the 22-strong field moved away from their grid slots on intermediate tyres.

“I can’t accelerate! It’s not working, guys,” said Verstappen.

A few moments later, Hamilton ground to a halt on the start/finish straight.

With more cars encountering problems, having been lapping much more slowly than usual, Race Control felt there was no option but to suspend the starting procedure and throw a red flag – the drivers returning to the pit lane and waiting for a second attempt at a start.

“There’s still a bit of spray; I think we have to stay out,” reported Verstappen on the latest formation lap, while Gasly dropped his car through Turn 5, slid over the grass and just about collected it. “It’s so slippery, guys,” said fellow soft-starter Hamilton.

One lap later, Piastri, Bortoleto, Stroll and Hulkenberg did the same. Race Control then confirmed a standing start, with the Safety Car duly peeling into the pits and setting up the prospect of a thrilling run down to Turn 1.

Back at the front, Antonelli had built a lead of a couple of seconds over team mate Russell, who was then caught by Verstappen and overtaken into Turn 4.

“There’s smoke, like fire.

“It does not seem to be drying rapidly. It’s weird,” reported Russell, who was gradually falling away from Verstappen and Antonelli.

Just as the Dutchman was looking for a way past, slick-shod Bottas spun off the track in the final sector and triggered a Safety Car – bringing the intermediate runners into the pits for a switch to slick tyres.

After a few laps behind the Safety Car, the race resumed and the battle for the lead resumed. Verstappen tucked into Antonelli’s slipstream as they headed onto Lap 13 and launched a bold move around the outside of Turn 1, which he completed at the exit of Turn 2.

Meanwhile, Verstappen was pumping in a series of fastest laps and leaving the pair behind – his gap over Russell above three seconds by Lap 19.

Verstappen, though, was now some five seconds up the road.

Antonelli’s attempts to leave Russell behind and reel in Verstappen were hampered when he ran wide at the final corner and clipped the pit entry bollard. “Check the front wing,” he asked over the radio, with Russell now just one second behind, and Verstappen moving eight seconds clear.

“Why have we pulled the trigger so early?”

On Lap 43, the Virtual Safety Car was deployed due to Albon stopping out on track in his Williams, prompting extra pit stops from Verstappen and Hamilton.

A lap later, however, Antonelli also pitted for fresh tyres, along with team mate Russell, returning P1 to Verstappen. As marshals worked to move Albon’s car, a full Safety Car was deployed, prompting stops from Norris, Lawson, Alonso and Hulkenberg.

Disaster struck for Russell as the field circulated behind the Safety Car – the Briton grinding to a halt just before Turn 1 and dropping out of the race. “Ahhh!”

When the race resumed, Verstappen nailed his restart to maintain P1 over Antonelli and Hadjar, with Hamilton and Leclerc hovering in fourth and fifth, and Piastri surviving an attack from Lawson to keep hold of sixth.

Verstappen controlled the final few kilometres to take the chequered flag a couple of seconds up on Antonelli, with Hamilton, Leclerc and Hadjar also maintaining formation, Piastri taking sixth, Lawson seventh and Alonso eighth.

# Verstappen wins rain-hit Bahrain GP in Malaysia over Antonelli as Russell retires late on

Max Verstappen claimed his and Red Bull’s first win of the 2026 season at the end of a dramatic, rain-delayed Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

Oct 04, 2026 10:38am UTC

![KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 04: Race winner Max Verstappen of the Netherlands and Oracle Red](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9North/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/trackside-images/2026/F1_Grand_Prix_of_Bahrain_in_Malaysia/2298510158.webp)

Max Verstappen converted pole position into victory during Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, which was impacted by heavy rain, featured an entertaining crossover from intermediate tyres to slicks, and saw overtaking from start to finish – as well as a dramatic late retirement for George Russell.

After a delayed start and then a suspended start procedure, as several drivers struggled to maintain speed on the initial formation lap, the race eventually got under way in slippery, mixed conditions – leading to split tyre strategies and plenty of early action.

Polesitter Verstappen fell behind Mercedes pair Kimi Antonelli and Russell on the run down to Turn 1, with all three drivers running intermediate tyres, but he soon settled into a rhythm and managed to pick off the Silver Arrows either side of a Safety Car that was deployed when Valtteri Bottas spun out.

That Safety Car period represented the ideal window for the intermediate starters to switch to slick tyres, with those who lined up on slick compounds getting caught out, and threats of further rain not materialising before the chequered flag.

Verstappen controlled proceedings after working his way back into P1, pulling away from Antonelli and Russell – who had their own battle over second – and navigating a late Virtual Safety Car/Safety Car combination to secure his and Red Bull’s breakthrough first win of the 2026 campaign.

Antonelli was already set to extend his championship lead over Russell by three points when his team mate dramatically ground to a halt on the start/finish straight behind that final Safety Car, dealing another blow to the Briton's already slim title chances.

Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc were high-profile names to start the race on slick tyres, with both drivers dropping towards the back of the grid as a result. However, inspired comeback drives saw them recover to P3 and P4 respectively, and bag a healthy haul of points for Ferrari.

Isack Hadjar dropped from third to fifth in the closing laps as Hamilton and Leclerc completed their charges, ahead of McLaren’s Oscar Piastri in P6, Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson in P7 and Fernando Alonso in a morale-boosting P8 for Aston Martin.

![](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9Centre/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/fom-website/2026/Bahrain%20(Malaysia)/race%20start%20bahrain%2026.webp)The Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia saw action from start to finish

Lando Norris sat on team mate Piastri’s tail before the final restart, only to lose control of his McLaren behind the Safety Car and run through the gravel, leaving him to settle for ninth, in front of Racing Bulls rookie and final points finisher Arvid Lindblad.

As has so often been the case this season, Audi driver Nico Hulkenberg just missed out on a reward in 11th, followed by the other Aston Martin of Lance Stroll, Alpine’s Franco Colapinto and the Haas machines of Ollie Bearman and Esteban Ocon.

Pierre Gasly almost crashed out during the formation lap on slick tyres, but managed to rejoin the action and eventually finish 16th, ahead of Williams’ Carlos Sainz and Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto, who were involved in a mid-race collision (for which the latter was penalised).

Cadillac’s Sergio Perez was the day’s final finisher in 19th position, given the aforementioned Russell’s heartache, Bottas’ race-ending spin, and another stoppage involving the Williams of Alex Albon, which brought out the late Safety Car.

![KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 04: Max Verstappen of the Netherlands and Oracle Red Bull Racing](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9North/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/trackside-images/2026/F1_Grand_Prix_of_Bahrain_in_Malaysia/2298485807.webp)Verstappen and Red Bull claimed pole for the first time in 2026 at Sepang

### AS IT HAPPENED

At the end of an entertaining Qualifying session around the Sepang International Circuit, it was Verstappen who grabbed his and Red Bull’s first pole position of the 2026 season, just ahead of Ferrari rival Hamilton.

Hadjar had rounded out the top three positions in the sister Red Bull, but subsequently took a five-place grid penalty for using extra power unit elements, promoting Mercedes driver championship leader Antonelli to third, and Ferrari’s Leclerc to fourth.

Elsewhere, Alpine’s Colapinto and Racing Bulls’ Lindblad dropped to the very back of the grid. Colapinto served a five-place penalty for his Turn 1 collision in Azerbaijan last time out, coupled with a 10-place drop for taking on new power unit elements, while Lindblad also fitted new PU components, resulting in a combined 30-place demotion.

With that grid-deciding session out of the way, attention soon turned to Sunday’s 56-lap Grand Prix, and how many pit stops drivers might need to make given the high levels of tyre degradation witnessed in practice – Pirelli predicting either a two- or three-stop race.

But then, in the hour before lights out, a huge rain shower – and accompanying thunderstorm – soaked the circuit, adding a completely different dimension to the mix. Would the race get under way as planned? Or would there be a delay to proceedings?

![KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 04: Rain falls in the Pitlane prior to the F1 Grand Prix of](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9Centre/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/trackside-images/2026/F1_Grand_Prix_of_Bahrain_in_Malaysia/2298485861.webp)Rain poured down ahead of the race start in Malaysia

That was answered a couple of minutes before the scheduled start of 1500 local time, when Race Control confirmed a delay – the rain still pouring down, and teams sheltering their multi-million dollar cars on the starting grid with gazebos.

An exploratory lap by the Medical Car highlighted just how tricky the conditions had become, as it slid its way around the track and subsequently reported a significant amount of standing water, which meant conditions were not currently suitable to start the race.

At around 1510 local time, the rain appeared to ease slightly, bringing cheers from the grandstands and grass banks lining the track, which only grew louder when the Medical Car appeared for another assessment.

By 1525, F1’s governing body, the FIA, reported that only a couple of corners were still an issue, thanks to a combination of lighter rainfall and the marshals sweeping the track to remove as much standing water as possible.

A few minutes later, it was announced that the formation lap would take place at 1540. This led to a flurry of activity as drivers who had been sheltering in the pit lane and paddock headed to the grid and got strapped back into their cars.

![KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 04: The FIA Safety Car leads  Max Verstappen of the Netherlands](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9South/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/trackside-images/2026/F1_Grand_Prix_of_Bahrain_in_Malaysia/2298488848.webp)The initial start procedure was suspended when several drivers hit trouble

So, some 40 minutes later than planned, the 22-strong field moved away from their grid slots on intermediate tyres. According to Race Control, there would be a minimum of two laps behind the Safety Car before a standing start – subject to change based on driver feed.

There was drama almost immediately when Hadjar lost control of his Red Bull exiting Turn 2 and took a trip through the gravel, before Verstappen and then Hamilton appeared to encounter power issues. “I can’t accelerate! It’s not working, guys,” said Verstappen. Hamilton, meanwhile, reported: ”I’m pressing the throttle and nothing’s happening!”

A few moments later, Hamilton ground to a halt on the start/finish straight. “It’s a software issue \[that\] we’re trying to solve,” the seven-time World Champion was told by the Ferrari pit wall. He eventually got going again, but was now massively out of position.

With more cars encountering problems, having been lapping much more slowly than usual, Race Control felt there was no option but to suspend the starting procedure and throw a red flag – the drivers returning to the pit lane and waiting for a second attempt at a start.

That second attempt was eventually scheduled for 1633, with the original grid order in play. So, it would be Verstappen in P1 from Hamilton, Antonelli, Leclerc, the McLarens, Russell and Hadjar, who had managed to escape from the gravel on the first formation lap.

![KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 04: Fans shelter underneath umbrellas as they look on from a](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9South/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/trackside-images/2026/F1_Grand_Prix_of_Bahrain_in_Malaysia/2298511696.webp)Drivers and fans waited patiently after the first start procedure was suspended

The next question was around tyres, and the choice between intermediates or slicks given how much the track had dried up. It was soon revealed that plenty of drivers were on intermediates. However, Hamilton, Leclerc, Gasly, Bortoleto, Hulkenberg, Bearman, Bottas, Perez and Colapinto all went for softs, and Norris, Piastri, Alonso and Stroll bolted on mediums.

“There’s still a bit of spray; I think we have to stay out,” reported Verstappen on the latest formation lap, while Gasly dropped his car through Turn 5, slid over the grass and just about collected it. “It’s so slippery, guys,” said fellow soft-starter Hamilton.

Perez was the only driver to pit at the end of the first lap behind the Safety Car, swapping to intermediates. One lap later, Piastri, Bortoleto, Stroll and Hulkenberg did the same. Race Control then confirmed a standing start, with the Safety Car duly peeling into the pits and setting up the prospect of a thrilling run down to Turn 1.

When the lights went out, with Perez pitting for a second time, Antonelli and Russell charged off the line to take P1 and P2 for Mercedes, while Lawson surged to third and engaged in a wheel-to-wheel battle with polesitter Verstappen.

Hadjar was up to fifth, ahead of Williams pair Sainz and Albon, the Haas of Ocon, the Racing Bulls machine of Lindblad, and the McLaren of Piastri, with Hamilton and Leclerc pushed out of the top 10 places on their slick tyres.

As that tumble down the order continued, Leclerc decided to ditch his soft tyres for intermediates, while team mate Hamilton ploughed on and tried to make it work. A bit of back-and-forth followed between Hamilton and the Ferrari pit wall, before they settled on sticking with their “gamble”.

Back at the front, Antonelli had built a lead of a couple of seconds over team mate Russell, who was then caught by Verstappen and overtaken into Turn 4. Hadjar also made a move in the other Red Bull by clearing Lawson for P4 into the final corner.

Ocon had made some more progress to run sixth, ahead of Sainz, back-row starter Lindblad and Albon, with Piastri completing the points-paying places, over Bortoleto, Hulkenberg, Stroll, Perez, Norris and Alonso – the latter two having stuck with their medium tyres.

“There’s smoke, like fire. I don’t know if it’s coming from my car or not,” said Bortoleto over the radio as he tried to keep in touch with Piastri. Replays then showed that Leclerc had damaged his front wing with the other Audi of Hulkenberg at the start, which lengthened the Monegasque’s pit stop as a change was made.

So, with the race settling down, how much longer would the track remain more favourable to intermediate tyres? “It does not seem to be drying rapidly. It’s weird,” reported Russell, who was gradually falling away from Verstappen and Antonelli.

![KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 04:  Max Verstappen of the Netherlands driving the (3) Oracle Red](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9North/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/trackside-images/2026/F1_Grand_Prix_of_Bahrain_in_Malaysia/2298504637.webp)Verstappen fought back and reclaimed positions from the Mercedes drivers

At the end of Lap 8, and heading onto Lap 9, Antonelli drifted wide at the final corner to open the door for Verstappen. Just as the Dutchman was looking for a way past, slick-shod Bottas spun off the track in the final sector and triggered a Safety Car – bringing the intermediate runners into the pits for a switch to slick tyres.

Mercedes pulled off a perfect stop under pressure to keep Antonelli ahead of Verstappen, while Russell maintained position over Hadjar, Lawson, Ocon, Lindblad, Sainz, Bortoleto and Piastri. Stroll beat Albon out of the pit lane for P1, from Hulkenberg and Perez, with Hamilton, Norris and Leclerc back in 15th, 16th and 17th respectively. Alonso, Bearman, Gasly and Colapinto were the final runners at this stage.

After a few laps behind the Safety Car, the race resumed and the battle for the lead resumed. Verstappen tucked into Antonelli’s slipstream as they headed onto Lap 13 and launched a bold move around the outside of Turn 1, which he completed at the exit of Turn 2. Russell then brilliantly took advantage of the squabbling to snatch P2 from Antonelli through Turn 5.

Around that time, the stewards noted a Turn 2 incident involving Bortoleto and Sainz – the Williams driver tipped into a spin and dropping from the top 10 to 18th position, and the Audi man pitting shortly afterwards with damage. That aided Hamilton’s recovery towards the points, as he inherited 10th before clearing Hulkenberg for ninth.

“I have more pace,” claimed Antonelli over the radio after a few tours in Russell’s dirty air. “We’ll do something different,” was the reply from Mercedes, referring to strategy. Meanwhile, Verstappen was pumping in a series of fastest laps and leaving the pair behind – his gap over Russell above three seconds by Lap 19.

At the start of Lap 21, Antonelli had arrived on the back of team mate Russell’s car. After a look through Turns 1 and 2, the young Italian reclaimed P2 with a smart move into Turn 4. Verstappen, though, was now some five seconds up the road.

Hamilton continued his comeback with a series of moves on Lindblad, Ocon and Lawson, which put him fifth. Piastri was ninth, unable to make the same kind of progress, with Leclerc now 10th and Norris 11th – Hulkenberg nudged out of the points in the process.

Antonelli’s attempts to leave Russell behind and reel in Verstappen were hampered when he ran wide at the final corner and clipped the pit entry bollard. “Check the front wing,” he asked over the radio, with Russell now just one second behind, and Verstappen moving eight seconds clear.

At the back of the field, Bortoleto was now under investigation for his collision with Sainz, while Albon had also been noted for driving erratically – an incident that will be properly assessed by the stewarding panel post-race.

TV coverage then cut to Hadjar, and a heated radio exchange with his engineer. Informed about Hamilton closing rapidly and being quicker throughout the lap, he shared his frustration and shouted that he was “done”. Behind, Piastri was up to sixth over Lawson, while Norris held eighth, as more midfield pit stops took place.

![KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 04: Lando Norris of Great Britain driving the (1) McLaren MCL40](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9Centre/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/trackside-images/2026/F1_Grand_Prix_of_Bahrain_in_Malaysia/2298509028.webp)There were overtakes left, right and centre throughout the race

Russell was the first of the top three runners to make his planned final stop on Lap 33, with Verstappen and Antonelli following a lap later – all three taking softs. “Why have we pulled the trigger so early?” Russell commented over the radio, after being told he would not be stopping again.

“This tyre feels terrible,” came another tyre-related message from the medium-shod Hamilton, who had nonetheless closed up to the rear of Hadjar’s car and was pushing to take P4. Leclerc was up to sixth in the other Ferrari, from Lawson, Piastri, Norris and Lindblad.

Fresh from a pit stop, and running soft tyres, Hulkenberg caught the eye with a double pass on Stroll and Ocon into Turn 4. The German was also noted for a potentially unsafe release in the pit lane, though, while team mate Bortoleto took a 10-second penalty for his clash with Sainz.

On Lap 43, the Virtual Safety Car was deployed due to Albon stopping out on track in his Williams, prompting extra pit stops from Verstappen and Hamilton. As he rejoined the action, Verstappen dropped to second, behind Antonelli – his 12-second margin not enough to retain the lead.

A lap later, however, Antonelli also pitted for fresh tyres, along with team mate Russell, returning P1 to Verstappen. As marshals worked to move Albon’s car, a full Safety Car was deployed, prompting stops from Norris, Lawson, Alonso and Hulkenberg.

![KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 04: Lewis Hamilton of Great Britain driving the (44) Scuderia](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9South/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/trackside-images/2026/F1_Grand_Prix_of_Bahrain_in_Malaysia/2298495147.webp)Hamilton and Leclerc recovered well after losing lots of ground at the start

Disaster struck for Russell as the field circulated behind the Safety Car – the Briton grinding to a halt just before Turn 1 and dropping out of the race. “Ahhh!” Russell shouted over the radio, with his outside chance of fighting for the title taking a huge hit.

Meanwhile, with the cars ahead bunching up, Norris came close to slamming into the back of team mate Piastri’s car under braking for the first corner. He took to the run-off at speed, slid through the gravel and rejoined the queue down in 11th.

When the race resumed, Verstappen nailed his restart to maintain P1 over Antonelli and Hadjar, with Hamilton and Leclerc hovering in fourth and fifth, and Piastri surviving an attack from Lawson to keep hold of sixth. Alonso and Hulkenberg were eighth and ninth, with Norris passing Lindblad to get back into the points.

A lap later, Hamilton sent the crowd wild by passing Hadjar into Turn 1 for third, capping off an impressive rise from the back of the grid. Leclerc followed suit at the start of the next tour, turning an initially dire race for Ferrari into something much more positive.

![KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 04: George Russell of Great Britain and Mercedes AMG Petronas F1](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9North/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/trackside-images/2026/F1_Grand_Prix_of_Bahrain_in_Malaysia/2298507420.webp)Russell could not believe his luck as he stopped out on track in the closing laps

Verstappen controlled the final few kilometres to take the chequered flag a couple of seconds up on Antonelli, with Hamilton, Leclerc and Hadjar also maintaining formation, Piastri taking sixth, Lawson seventh and Alonso eighth.

Hulkenberg dropped out of the points late on and wound up 11th, behind Norris and Lindblad, while Stroll took 12th in his Aston Martin, Colapinto placed 13th and the Haas cars of Bearman and Ocon took 14th and 15th – the latter starting the race so well but losing out as various strategies and Safety Cars played out.

Gasly was 16th in the second of the Alpine cars, from Sainz, the penalised Bortoleto and Perez as the final finisher. Russell, Albon and Bottas were the three drivers who failed to finish – the former’s being particularly tough to take.

Russell had trimmed Antonelli’s lead to 66 points after victory in Azerbaijan, but his DNF and Antonelli’s second-place finish means that is back up to 84 points heading into the final seven rounds of the season.

![KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA - OCTOBER 04: Race winner Max Verstappen of the Netherlands and Oracle Red](https://media.formula1.com/image/upload/t_16by9South/c_lfill,w_3392/q_auto/v1740000001/trackside-images/2026/F1_Grand_Prix_of_Bahrain_in_Malaysia/2298514236.webp)Sunday at Sepang belonged to Verstappen and Red Bull

### Key quote

“It’s a really nice one, after the year that we’ve had and the progression that we’ve made,” said Verstappen. “I’m incredibly proud of everyone, and it’s just super nice to win here. It was very hectic with a lot of different things in the start. No power, so you have to wait for the power to kick in. But then we made the right call with the intermediates, and after that, step by step, we moved our way forward. From there onwards we could do our own race until the end again, of course, with the Safety Car, but we kept it all under control.”

### What’s next

The Singapore Grand Prix hosts the final stop of this triple header sequence on October 9-11. Head to the [RACE HUB](https://www.formula1.com/en/racing/2026/singapore) to find out how you can follow the action from the Marina Bay Street Circuit.

# Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 Malaysia Race Report: Verstappen Wins as Ford Ends 23-Year Wait

![Terry Widdows, Founder and Editor of Coffee Corner Motorsport](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/f23ded502c558b50f9c9d0a0ff129af30a37696b6278825c24fd5a9e6d32ac42?s=54&d=mm&r=g)

Written by [Terry Widdows - Coffee Corner Motorsport](https://coffeecornermotorsport.com/author/terrycoffeecornermotorsport-com/)

4 October 2026 · 12:03 BST

**_Max Verstappen won the Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 at Sepang, the first win for Red Bull Ford Powertrains and Ford’s first Formula 1 victory since 2003, on a day that nearly never got started. Heavy rain delayed the start, then the formation laps were red-flagged when several cars lost power, with the problems suspected to be software-related. Racing finally got underway 93 minutes late. Verstappen bogged down at the standing start, recovered on intermediates, took the lead at the Lap 13 restart and held it to the flag, 2.307 seconds clear of Kimi Antonelli. George Russell’s power unit failure behind the Safety Car on Lap 50 took him out of third and stretched Antonelli’s championship lead to 84 points. Ferrari looked to have thrown it away early, with Lewis Hamilton nearly stopping on the formation lap and Charles Leclerc running last on Lap 5. They left with third and fourth._**

![Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 Malaysia race report – Max Verstappen celebrates victory at Sepang © Getty Images / Red Bull Content Pool](https://coffeecornermotorsport.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/SI202610040308.webp)_**Max Verstappen celebrates in parc ferme after winning the Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 in Malaysia at Sepang. © Getty Images / Red Bull Content Pool**_

* * *

### **Key Points: Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 Malaysia Race Report**

- Winner: Max Verstappen (Red Bull) from pole, 2.307 seconds clear of Antonelli. First win for Red Bull Ford Powertrains, Ford’s first F1 win since the 2003 Brazilian Grand Prix, and Verstappen’s first win of 2026
- Start chaos: formation laps red-flagged after Verstappen, Hamilton, Lawson, Bortoleto and Bottas hit power problems, suspected to be software-related. Original grid restored. Racing began 93 minutes late
- Title swing: Russell retires from third with a power unit issue behind the Safety Car on Lap 50. Antonelli takes 18 points, and his lead grows to 84
- Ferrari recovery: Hamilton P3 after losing power on the formation lap and dropping to tenth on slicks. Leclerc P4 after running last on Lap 5
- Hadjar P5, Piastri P6, Lawson P7. Alonso holds off Norris for eighth on the final lap. Lindblad passes Hülkenberg on the last lap for the final point
- Retirements: Bottas spins off on Lap 9, Albon stops with a gearbox failure on Lap 43, Russell out on Lap 50

## **Race Recap: Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 Malaysia Race Report**

### Before the Lights: Rain, Red Flag, Reset

A tropical thunderstorm hit Sepang before the start and left standing water across the circuit. Race control held the start while the Medical Car reported back, sweepers and marshals cleared the worst of it, and the field waited. F1’s first wet race under the 2026 regulations. Nobody on the grid had raced this generation of car in the wet.

The formation laps got going behind the Safety Car, with Verstappen leading from pole. Then the cars started failing. Verstappen reported a lack of acceleration before getting going again. Hamilton, second on the grid, lost power completely and crawled round as the field went past him, telling his team nothing was happening when he pressed the throttle. Lawson was stuck on the grid. Bortoleto and Bottas struggled with similar problems. Hadjar slid into the gravel and rejoined.

Ferrari reset Hamilton’s software and he got going again. The order was a mess by then. Race control suspended the start procedure, threw the red flag and brought everyone into the pit lane. The problems hit cars with Red Bull Ford, Ferrari and Audi power units, and were suspected to be software-related. At the time of writing, the FIA hadn’t issued a statement on the cause. Race control confirmed the original grid would stand, so Hamilton got his second place back.

By the time a start time came, the rain had stopped and the track was drying fast. Free tyre choice. Verstappen, both Mercedes and most of the field went for intermediates. Hamilton and Leclerc went for softs. Norris and Piastri went for mediums. The race got going at 16:33 local time, 93 minutes after the original start.

### The Start: Slicks Go Backwards, Mercedes Go Forwards

Two laps behind the Safety Car, then a standing start on Lap 3. Gasly had already spun on softs behind the Safety Car. Perez came in for intermediates. Piastri pitted to get off his mediums before the start. Bortoleto pitted too.

Verstappen didn’t get away. Neither did anyone on slicks. Antonelli led into Turn 1 from Russell, a Mercedes one-two on the intermediates. Lawson made a brilliant start and fought Verstappen. Hadjar was up to fifth. Hamilton was the first of the slick runners, down in tenth.

Verstappen was third by Lap 4 and through on Russell on Lap 6. Ferrari’s afternoon looked finished. Leclerc came in for intermediates on Lap 4, had a very slow stop and dropped to last. Hamilton and Norris stayed out on slicks, both already more than a pit stop behind.

### Lap 9: Bottas Spins, Safety Car, Slick Switch

Verstappen was 0.7 seconds behind Antonelli on Lap 8. On Lap 9 Antonelli ran wide at the final corner and only just held on in the drag race to Turn 1. Then Bottas lost the rear on softs and went into the gravel. Full Safety Car, called before the leaders reached the final corner. Perfect timing for slicks.

Everyone on intermediates came in. Antonelli and Russell went to mediums. Verstappen and Hadjar went to softs. Lawson took hards. Hamilton stayed out on his original softs and kept the track position. On the way into the pits, Piastri nearly got caught out by a slow-moving Albon ahead of him. The stewards will look at that one after the race.

### Lap 13: Verstappen Takes It

Verstappen, on softs, went round the outside of Antonelli into Turn 1 and had him into Turn 2. Russell followed him through as Antonelli wobbled off the racing line. Behind, Bortoleto went down the inside of Sainz at Turn 2 and tagged the Williams into a spin. 10-second time penalty for Bortoleto. Sainz dropped down the order.

Antonelli wasn’t happy on the mediums at first and dropped back from his team mate. By Lap 19 he was telling the team he had more pace. On Lap 21 he went past Russell into Turn 4. Russell didn’t fight it hard. Verstappen was already over four seconds up the road.

Hamilton was coming. Eleventh on Lap 15 on the same set of softs he started on, he cleared Piastri and Lindblad by Lap 20, Ocon on Lap 21 and Lawson on Lap 24 for fifth. Leclerc was back up to ninth.

Antonelli’s one slip came on Lap 25. He went too deep into the final corner, clipped the bollard at the pit lane entry and asked the team to check his front wing. Verstappen’s lead went out to 7.4 seconds and then 8.8 by Lap 29.

### The Pit Window: Verstappen Out of Sight

Leclerc pitted for used softs on Lap 29. Hadjar and Hamilton came in together on Lap 32, Red Bull covering the Ferrari. Russell pitted on Lap 33 for softs, then Verstappen and Antonelli on Lap 34, both on softs. Hamilton ended up on used mediums, told they had to go to the end, and said they felt terrible.

Verstappen led by 10.2 seconds on Lap 36 and 12 seconds by Lap 43. Hadjar held Hamilton off for lap after lap in fourth. It looked done.

### Lap 43: Albon Stops, Race Flips

Albon parked up with a broken gearbox right by a gap in the barriers. Virtual Safety Car. Verstappen pitted from the lead for used softs. Antonelli and Russell stayed out for track position, and Antonelli led the race.

It didn’t last. Mercedes boxed both cars under the VSC on Lap 45. On Lap 46 the full Safety Car was called, with a tractor needed to move the Williams. Verstappen was back in front, Antonelli second, Russell third. Hamilton and Leclerc pitted too, Hamilton taking used softs, and Hadjar came in again to cover him. Piastri and Norris were the last of the front runners to stop.

### Lap 50: Russell Parks Up

Still behind the Safety Car, Russell pulled over on the main straight. Hands on his helmet. Mercedes said it was a power unit issue. In the same moment Norris, caught out by the leaders backing up, slid off into the gravel. He rejoined but wasn’t allowed to retake the places under the Safety Car and dropped to 11th.

Antonelli was straight on the radio asking what had happened. The team said they would diagnose it later. Russell was third and on course for big points. He leaves Sepang with nothing.

### The Final Sprint: Ferrari Finish the Job

The race went green on Lap 52 with 19 minutes left on the race clock, more than three hours after it was due to start. Verstappen got the restart right and was clean away from Antonelli, who was cautious with his team mate out.

Then Ferrari finished the comeback. Hamilton went past Hadjar down the main straight on Lap 53 for third. One lap later Leclerc took Hadjar into Turn 1 for fourth. The car that was last on Lap 5 finished fourth.

Norris fought back into the points, clearing Lindblad and then Hülkenberg, and chased Alonso to the line. Alonso held him off for eighth, a rare points finish for Aston Martin. Lindblad got Hülkenberg on the last lap for tenth.

Verstappen crossed the line 2.307 seconds clear of Antonelli. Hamilton third, 4.919 seconds back. Verstappen won the last Malaysian Grand Prix at Sepang in 2017. Nine years later, he won there again.

## **From the Podium: Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 Malaysia Race Report**

> _“I’m incredibly proud of everyone. It was very hectic, with a lot of different things. We made the right call with the inters, and after that, step by step, we moved forward and could so our own race until the end and we kept it all under control.”_
>
> **Max Verstappen, Red Bull**

> _“I think today was the maximum we could have done, massive congrats to Max and Red Bull for their incredible weekend. On our side, work to do but happy to come away with P2. Hopefully we will come back in the future to Malaysia.”_
>
> **Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes**

> _“Big congratulations to Max, what a tough race that was. Obviously, we had the wrong call at the beginning which was so difficult. I could see everyone pulling away, I was a minute down and I just got my head down. Honestly, of all the years I’ve been here, this is the best race we’ve had here.”_
>
> **Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari**

## **Coffee Corner Take**

Red Bull Ford Powertrains has won a Grand Prix.

After years of winning with Honda power, Red Bull built its own engine for 2026 with Ford as partner. Fifteen rounds of chasing. Verstappen arrived at Sepang sixth in the championship without a win all season, put the car on pole on Saturday and won with it on Sunday. Ford’s last win came at the 2003 Brazilian Grand Prix with Fisichella and Jordan, another wet race ended by a red flag. Twenty-three years later it comes back in the rain.

The formation laps sit awkwardly next to that. Red Bull Ford cars were among those that lost power, Verstappen’s included, along with cars powered by Ferrari and Audi, and the whole start had to be red-flagged. At the time of writing the FIA hasn’t said why. One of the engines that cut out before the start went on to win the race. That needs an answer.

Ferrari’s start was a mess. Both cars on softs while the leaders went for intermediates, and Hamilton said it himself afterwards: the wrong call. He was a minute down. Leclerc pitted for intermediates, lost time with a slow stop and was last on Lap 5.

Then they salvaged it. Ferrari left Hamilton out on his original softs under the Safety Car and he started picking cars off, eleventh on Lap 15 and fifth by Lap 24. Leclerc came through from the back. Both of them got Hadjar in the last three laps for third and fourth. Hamilton called it the best race he’s had at Sepang, and he’s now 22 points behind Russell for second in the championship.

Russell is the one who pays for today. He won in Baku last time out and was running third here, until the power unit failed behind the Safety Car with five laps to go. Zero points. Mercedes now have a reliability question to answer on top of a weekend where Red Bull had the pace.

Antonelli didn’t win and didn’t need to. Mediums he didn’t like early on and a clip of the pit entry bollard on Lap 25 didn’t stop him bringing it home second without taking a risk at the final restart. He came in 66 clear and leaves with 84.

Verstappen had won at least one race every season since 2016, and 2026 was running out of time to keep that going. He bogged down at the standing start, came back on intermediates and won by over two seconds at the circuit where he won in 2017.

Antonelli leads on 320. Russell is 84 behind on 236, with Hamilton 22 further back and closing on second.

Max Verstappen held off Kimi Antonelli to win the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia — his first victory of this F1 season — on a chaotic day that began with the race delayed 90 minutes by rain and software issues with some drivers' cars.

Verstappen leaped into his teammates' arms after exiting the car following his 72nd career victory.

"It's a really nice one after the year that we've had and the progression we made," Verstappen said.

"What the f*** happened?"

Antonelli leads the season with 320 points to Russell's 236. Verstappen has 188 after his victory, which followed a pair of second-place podiums.

Verstappen came into the day having won his first pole of the season a week after he lost the Azerbaijan Grand Prix by less than two-tenths of a second to Russell.

Heavy rain in Malaysia, however, delayed the start of Sunday's race, and then when the drivers did get going … some of them didn't get going.

The race was red-flagged while teams attended to the software issues. The original grid was then used — even though some cars had been out of place at the time of the red flag — when the race restarted.

"It was a very hectic start with a number of different things," Verstappen said.

"What a tough race that was," Hamilton said, summing up the day's events.

Max Verstappen held off Kimi Antonelli to win the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia — his first victory of this F1 season — on a chaotic day that began with the race delayed 90 minutes by rain and software issues with some drivers' cars.

Antonelli, the season's points leader, took second while Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton completed a remarkable comeback from more than a minute down to finish third.

Verstappen leaped into his teammates' arms after exiting the car following his 72nd career victory. He was able to keep Antonelli at bay without a true challenge, despite a race restart with only about four laps to go.

"It's a really nice one after the year that we've had and the progression we made," Verstappen said.

George Russell, Antonelli's Mercedes teammate and a preseason favorite, dropped out of the race when his car had mechanical issues around lap 49 while the safety car was out.

"What the f\*\*\* happened?" Antonelli said after Russell's car came to a halt.

Antonelli leads the season with 320 points to Russell's 236. Hamilton is in third with 214. Verstappen has 188 after his victory, which followed a pair of second-place podiums.

Verstappen came into the day having won his first pole of the season a week after he lost the Azerbaijan Grand Prix by less than two-tenths of a second to Russell.

Heavy rain in Malaysia, however, delayed the start of Sunday's race, and then when the drivers did get going … some of them didn't get going. Hamilton, among others, quickly reported a loss of power in their cars during the formation lap.

"I'm pressing the throttle, and nothing is happening," Hamilton said before his car came to a stop on the back straight.

The race was red-flagged while teams attended to the software issues. The original grid was then used — even though some cars had been out of place at the time of the red flag — when the race restarted.

"It was a very hectic start with a number of different things," Verstappen said. "No power — we had to wait for the power to kick in."

Drivers also faced challenges with their tires due to the day's conditions. When Verstappen and Antonelli both pitted at the end of lap 33, the Red Bull driver had more than a 10-second lead.

After a virtual safety car — eventually updated to a full safety car — later came out, Verstappen then pitted again. Mercedes left its cars out on the track for another lap before pitting, allowing Antonelli to briefly have the lead before they pitted. Antonelli's subsequent pit put Verstappen back in front.

"What a tough race that was," Hamilton said, summing up the day's events.
